name: Beechcraft Twin Bonanza (Model 50)
summary: Powerful, large-engined light twin built 1951–1962, Beechcraft's first twin of the postwar era and the basis for the Queen Air; the US Army flew it as the L-23.

wings: Low, straight wing with large engines set well out from the fuselage
engines: Two big engines in deep, widely spaced nacelles
Two-blade props on most; main wheels stay partly exposed when retracted
fuselage: Short, deep cabin with a Bonanza-style sloping windshield
tail: Tall, upright, squared-off fin and rudder

tellTales: Big, widely spaced engines on a straight low wing
Short Bonanza-style cabin with a sloping windshield

confusedWith.howToTell: The Queen Air has a much longer, deeper fuselage with more windows; the Twin Bonanza is short and compact.
The Travel Air is much smaller with slim engines; the Twin Bonanza has big, deep, widely spaced nacelles.
The Baron has a swept fin and slim nacelles; the Twin Bonanza has an upright squared fin and big engines.
